response.title: Harborlight FY26 Results and a Sixth Site

segments.heading: The big picture
segments.text: Harborlight grew in fiscal year 2026. Now staff want the board to fund a sixth site. Start with the growth. Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites. A year earlier, it enrolled 936. Of this year's learners, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential. Another 389 were English language learners.

segments.heading: How learners did
segments.text: Learners made real progress. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels. The CASAS assessment measures that gain. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in the organization's history has seen more. A learner at the Riverside site said it best. Quote. "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring." End quote.

segments.heading: Who does the work
segments.text: Volunteers carry much of the teaching. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. On average, a tutor stayed for 14 months. Paid staff back up that work. Harborlight employs 11 full-time staff. Four of them are site coordinators. Together, tutors and staff keep all five sites running for learners.

segments.heading: Where the money went
segments.text: Now the money. Operating expenses for FY2026 came to $1,420,000. Programs took 81 percent of spending. The money came from several places. Foundation grants provided $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237 to serve.

segments.heading: The waitlist and the request
segments.text: Demand still beats space. At year end, 287 adults sat on the waitlist. Most of them were waiting for the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks. Staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. That budget adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They say it would cut the waitlist in half.

segments.heading: What the board must weigh
segments.text: One caution stands out. Treasurer Dev Patel reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months. The board asked staff for a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request. Staff will bring it to the October 21 board meeting. Board members also want a short deck about the sixth site to share with funders. The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. First, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners, and seventy-one earned a high school equivalency credential. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist, and the average wait was nine weeks. Third, staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 for a sixth site. Reserves stand at 3.2 months, short of the 4 month target.
